name: Colorado State University
header:
Colorado State University
United States · Mathematics PhD
Roster and rank verification handled separately
Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written
materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• Two letters satisfy math, but three referee contacts are mandatory.
• Do not mistake 2024-25 free application days for this cycle.
• Stipend is nine months; tuition and insurance benefits have conditions.

sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Bachelor’s must be completed by enrollment. Mathematics background and overall post-secondary GPA at
least 3.0 are expected; a mathematics major is not mandatory. A completed UChicago mathematics bachelor’s
fits the degree route; GPA and individual preparation remain to be assessed. International applications are
accepted. [s1] [s3]
Before submission; Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Create the Slate account using its temporary PIN, submit the application and fee, then complete supporting
materials. The portal checklist reports missing items; email notifications report missing materials and
completion. Three referee contacts must be supplied even though mathematics requires only two letters. [s1]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
No advance adviser agreement is listed. Faculty interests below support targeted contact, but current
willingness to supervise must be asked. [s1] [s5] [s9]
Cycle verification [Standing rule]
Standing February 1 application rule; September 2026 handbook supplies historical/current-year funding
information, not a 2027-28 funding commitment. [s1] [s2]

sections.title: Deadlines by stage
sections.text:
Academic application; Funding consideration; Reference receipt; Supporting documents [Standing
rule]
Fall entry only; February 1 is the complete-file deadline for admission and financial-support consideration. Late
supporting materials reduce prospects for a TA. No separate grace period or deadline time zone is published.
Official transcripts are required before or during the first enrolled semester to register for the second. [s1] [s3]
Test-score receipt [Standing rule]
If sending optional GRE scores, allow 3-4 weeks for processing and meet the February 1 completed-file
deadline. Required English scores must be official. [s1]
Accepting an offer [Unresolved]
Not established by the cited public admissions materials. Confirm in the current application or with graduate
admissions before relying on a rule.

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Standing rule]
Published minima: TOEFL 80, IELTS 6.5, PTE 58 or Duolingo 120. Official agency reporting is required, code
4075. No conditional admission for insufficient English; the page excludes several alternate/home formats,
including TOEFL Essentials/ITP/MyBest and IELTS General/Indicator. Revised 2026 TOEFL scale not stated on
this page. [s1]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
A recently earned U.S. degree qualifies for an English-test exception. The public mathematics wording does not
expressly say an unfinished UChicago degree qualifies at application; confirm timing and documentation. [s1]
GRE General; GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
Both General and Mathematics Subject GRE are optional. Use institution code 4075 if reporting; processing can
take 3-4 weeks. [s1]

sections.title: Academic records
sections.text:
Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
Upload all post-high-school transcripts, including the front, reverse and grading scale. Separate study-abroad
records are needed unless the sponsoring transcript lists every course, grade and credit. Unofficial records
suffice for review and first-semester enrollment; official records must arrive before second-semester
registration or dismissal may follow. [s1] [s3]
Mathematics-course list; Course descriptions [Standing rule]
Not listed as a separate required item on the public mathematics application checklist. This does not establish
whether the current portal permits an optional upload; exact prompt, length, formatting and upload/link rule
are not published. [s1]

sections.title: Recommendation letters
sections.text:
Number and type [Standing rule]
Mathematics requires TWO letters; Graduate School requires THREE referee contacts. The first two received
satisfy the mathematics letter requirement. No prescribed letter format. [s1]
Scholarship references [Standing rule]
Apply by February 1 for department support. No separate incoming scholarship essay or extra reference is
identified by the mathematics instructions; independent awards may have separate requirements not specified
there. [s1]
What sends the invitation [Unresolved]

final submission sends them. [s1]
Before versus after submission; Updating and reusing letters [Unresolved]

admissions before relying on a rule.
Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
The portal checklist and completion/missing-document notifications track application materials. A separate
referee-specific receipt message is not described. [s1]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Prior cycle]
September 2026 handbook: entering stipend USD 22,510 for nine months; after Part B qualifying survey, USD
23,752. Assistant calculus/precalculus director adds USD 691 per semester. These are 2026 handbook rates,
not a confirmed 2027-28 offer. Tuition benefits vary by appointment/FTE, residency and funding source.
Qualifying SHIP coverage requires appointment and enrollment conditions. [s2]
Years of support; Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
PhD funding normally lasts five years subject to funds, duties and satisfactory progress (including 3.0 GPA and
enrollment). Sixth-year requests are due February 1 before that fall. Half-time duties average 20 hours/week.
Insurance contribution needs at least a 25% appointment, five resident credits and SHIP enrollment; holding
fall and spring appointments can cover summer premium. [s2]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
International applicants are considered for financial support through the same department application. Exact
nonresident tuition coverage and fees must be checked in the offer; a general tuition benefit is not evidence
that every charge is covered. [s1] [s2]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
Apply by February 1 for department support. No separate incoming scholarship essay or extra reference is
identified by the mathematics instructions; independent awards may have separate requirements not specified
there. [s1]
Other funding routes [Unresolved]
Not established by the cited public admissions materials. Confirm in the current application or with graduate
admissions before relying on a rule.
Application fee [Standing rule]
USD 70 for international degree-seeking applicants; USD 60 domestic. [s1] [s3]
Fee waiver [Standing rule]
Automatic waivers apply to graduates of U.S. land-grant or accredited Colorado institutions, not UChicago by
that criterion. Documented military, Peace Corps, AmeriCorps or Fulbright affiliation may qualify. Submit the

application first, wait for the waiver-form link without paying, and use the same email. Allow four business
days; submit at least a week before the program deadline. Listed free days are 2024-25, not 2026-27. [s4]

sections.title: Conflicts and remaining checks
sections.text:
Conflicting sources [Conflict]
The 2022 handbook’s lower stipends are superseded for this report by September 2026 rates. Central free-day
materials mention a personal-history statement absent from the math checklist. Gillespie’s personal page
reports tenure in 2025 while the department index still says assistant professor. [s2] [s4] [s5] [s8]
Checks still needed [Unresolved]
Confirm Fall 2027 deadline/time zone, in-progress degree waiver, personal-history portal requirement, letter
invitation/update/reuse, commitment date, 2027-28 stipend and exact tuition/fees coverage. Faculty entries
include verified recent papers for Juul, Miranda, Duflot, Hulpke and Wilson; confirm individual supervision
capacity. [s1] [s2] [s3] [s5]

sections.title: Potential advisers and recent research
sections.text:
Algebraic / arithmetic geometry
Rachel Pries
Curves, abelian varieties, Galois theory, Newton polygons and Shimura varieties. [s5] [s6]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
Research evidence: 2026 · Data for Shimura varieties intersecting the Torelli locus
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
Jeffrey Achter
Abelian varieties in positive characteristic, algebraic cycles and arithmetic geometry. [s5] [s7]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
Research evidence: 2026 · Regular homomorphisms, with a twist
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
Renzo Cavalieri
Moduli of curves and enumerative/tropical geometry. [s6] [s9]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
Research evidence: 2025 · Mass formula for non-ordinary curves in one dimensional families
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
Rick Miranda
Algebraic geometry of surfaces, elliptic fibrations, linear systems and Mori cones; recent papers include
Coxeter-theoretic methods for blowups. [s5] [q12]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
Research evidence: 2026 · Coxeter theory for curves on blowups of P^r
Research-paper evidence. Publication year is as stated; an old paper is not proof of recent activity.
Jeanne Duflot
Algebraic geometry, equivariant cohomology and K-theory; recent work studies complex projective geometry
of frequency-difference-of-arrival curves. [s5] [q13]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.

Current author-submitted research about GAP and computer algebra software; this supplements the older university-hosted

Groups, algebras and computation; categorification of characteristic structures, tensor isomorphism and
Lie-algebra methods. [s5] [q14]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.

text:
Colorado State University
United States · Mathematics PhD
Roster and rank verification handled separately
Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written
materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• Two letters satisfy math, but three referee contacts are mandatory.
• Do not mistake 2024-25 free application days for this cycle.
• Stipend is nine months; tuition and insurance benefits have conditions.
Eligibility and preparation
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Bachelor’s must be completed by enrollment. Mathematics background and overall post-secondary GPA at
least 3.0 are expected; a mathematics major is not mandatory. A completed UChicago mathematics bachelor’s
fits the degree route; GPA and individual preparation remain to be assessed. International applications are
accepted. [s1] [s3]
Before submission; Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Create the Slate account using its temporary PIN, submit the application and fee, then complete supporting
materials. The portal checklist reports missing items; email notifications report missing materials and
completion. Three referee contacts must be supplied even though mathematics requires only two letters. [s1]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
No advance adviser agreement is listed. Faculty interests below support targeted contact, but current
willingness to supervise must be asked. [s1] [s5] [s9]
Cycle verification [Standing rule]
Standing February 1 application rule; September 2026 handbook supplies historical/current-year funding
information, not a 2027-28 funding commitment. [s1] [s2]
Deadlines by stage
Academic application; Funding consideration; Reference receipt; Supporting documents [Standing
rule]
Fall entry only; February 1 is the complete-file deadline for admission and financial-support consideration. Late
supporting materials reduce prospects for a TA. No separate grace period or deadline time zone is published.
Official transcripts are required before or during the first enrolled semester to register for the second. [s1] [s3]
Test-score receipt [Standing rule]
If sending optional GRE scores, allow 3-4 weeks for processing and meet the February 1 completed-file
deadline. Required English scores must be official. [s1]
Accepting an offer [Unresolved]
Not established by the cited public admissions materials. Confirm in the current application or with graduate
admissions before relying on a rule.

English and GRE
English requirement [Standing rule]
Published minima: TOEFL 80, IELTS 6.5, PTE 58 or Duolingo 120. Official agency reporting is required, code
4075. No conditional admission for insufficient English; the page excludes several alternate/home formats,
including TOEFL Essentials/ITP/MyBest and IELTS General/Indicator. Revised 2026 TOEFL scale not stated on
this page. [s1]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
A recently earned U.S. degree qualifies for an English-test exception. The public mathematics wording does not
expressly say an unfinished UChicago degree qualifies at application; confirm timing and documentation. [s1]
GRE General; GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
Both General and Mathematics Subject GRE are optional. Use institution code 4075 if reporting; processing can
take 3-4 weeks. [s1]
Academic records
Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
Upload all post-high-school transcripts, including the front, reverse and grading scale. Separate study-abroad
records are needed unless the sponsoring transcript lists every course, grade and credit. Unofficial records
suffice for review and first-semester enrollment; official records must arrive before second-semester
registration or dismissal may follow. [s1] [s3]
Mathematics-course list; Course descriptions [Standing rule]
Not listed as a separate required item on the public mathematics application checklist. This does not establish
whether the current portal permits an optional upload; exact prompt, length, formatting and upload/link rule
are not published. [s1]
Recommendation letters
Number and type [Standing rule]
Mathematics requires TWO letters; Graduate School requires THREE referee contacts. The first two received
satisfy the mathematics letter requirement. No prescribed letter format. [s1]
Scholarship references [Standing rule]
Apply by February 1 for department support. No separate incoming scholarship essay or extra reference is
identified by the mathematics instructions; independent awards may have separate requirements not specified
there. [s1]
What sends the invitation [Unresolved]
References receive emailed requests; the public mathematics guide does not identify whether saving details or
final submission sends them. [s1]
Before versus after submission; Updating and reusing letters [Unresolved]
Not established by the cited public admissions materials. Confirm in the current application or with graduate
admissions before relying on a rule.
Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
The portal checklist and completion/missing-document notifications track application materials. A separate
referee-specific receipt message is not described. [s1]
Written materials
Academic CV / resume [Standing rule]
CV or résumé is required as an upload. Public length, file type and formatting rules are not given. [s1] [s3]

Statement of purpose; Research-interest statement [Standing rule]
SOP required. Faithful prompt paraphrase: describe academic/professional interests, prospective contributions,
and how lived experiences have developed relevant skills. No published word/page cap, font or spacing; upload
rather than an external-link instruction. [s1]
Personal / background statement [Conflict]
The mathematics checklist does not identify a separate personal-history statement; the central
free-application-day instructions list one among materials. Whether it appears as a distinct mathematics portal
requirement, its prompt and limits require confirmation. [s1] [s4]
Research proposal; Writing sample / thesis / research summary; Publications list; Course-list
document; Other short answers / materials [Standing rule]
Not listed as a separate required item on the public mathematics application checklist. This does not establish
whether the current portal permits an optional upload; exact prompt, length, formatting and upload/link rule
are not published. [s1]
Scholarship essays [Standing rule]
Apply by February 1 for department support. No separate incoming scholarship essay or extra reference is
identified by the mathematics instructions; independent awards may have separate requirements not specified
there. [s1]
Funding and fees
Amount and coverage [Prior cycle]
September 2026 handbook: entering stipend USD 22,510 for nine months; after Part B qualifying survey, USD
23,752. Assistant calculus/precalculus director adds USD 691 per semester. These are 2026 handbook rates,
not a confirmed 2027-28 offer. Tuition benefits vary by appointment/FTE, residency and funding source.
Qualifying SHIP coverage requires appointment and enrollment conditions. [s2]
Years of support; Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
PhD funding normally lasts five years subject to funds, duties and satisfactory progress (including 3.0 GPA and
enrollment). Sixth-year requests are due February 1 before that fall. Half-time duties average 20 hours/week.
Insurance contribution needs at least a 25% appointment, five resident credits and SHIP enrollment; holding
fall and spring appointments can cover summer premium. [s2]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
International applicants are considered for financial support through the same department application. Exact
nonresident tuition coverage and fees must be checked in the offer; a general tuition benefit is not evidence
that every charge is covered. [s1] [s2]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
Apply by February 1 for department support. No separate incoming scholarship essay or extra reference is
identified by the mathematics instructions; independent awards may have separate requirements not specified
there. [s1]
Other funding routes [Unresolved]
Not established by the cited public admissions materials. Confirm in the current application or with graduate
admissions before relying on a rule.
Application fee [Standing rule]
USD 70 for international degree-seeking applicants; USD 60 domestic. [s1] [s3]
Fee waiver [Standing rule]
Automatic waivers apply to graduates of U.S. land-grant or accredited Colorado institutions, not UChicago by
that criterion. Documented military, Peace Corps, AmeriCorps or Fulbright affiliation may qualify. Submit the

application first, wait for the waiver-form link without paying, and use the same email. Allow four business
days; submit at least a week before the program deadline. Listed free days are 2024-25, not 2026-27. [s4]
Conflicts and remaining checks
Conflicting sources [Conflict]
The 2022 handbook’s lower stipends are superseded for this report by September 2026 rates. Central free-day
materials mention a personal-history statement absent from the math checklist. Gillespie’s personal page
reports tenure in 2025 while the department index still says assistant professor. [s2] [s4] [s5] [s8]
Checks still needed [Unresolved]
Confirm Fall 2027 deadline/time zone, in-progress degree waiver, personal-history portal requirement, letter
invitation/update/reuse, commitment date, 2027-28 stipend and exact tuition/fees coverage. Faculty entries
include verified recent papers for Juul, Miranda, Duflot, Hulpke and Wilson; confirm individual supervision
capacity. [s1] [s2] [s3] [s5]
